## Plan pl_003 — FAN Approach for Patrick Flynn's Parentage (q_001)

**Context:** Two completed plans (pl_001, pl_002) placed Patrick in Thomas Flynn's Schuylkill County household in 1850 and 1860, found his 1908 death certificate naming Thomas as father (secondary informant — son-in-law), and came up empty on probate. The proof sits at **Probable**. Every source so far is either indirect census co-residence or a derivative/secondary death-certificate assertion. This plan expands outward through Thomas Flynn's family, community, and legal records to find corroborating direct evidence.

---

| # | ID | Record type | Source | Date window | What it targets |
|---|-----|-------------|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| 1 | pli_007 | Census | FamilySearch | 1870 | Thomas Flynn's full household — names wife & siblings, maps the FAN cluster |
| 2 | pli_008 | Census | FamilySearch | 1880 | **First census with a relationship column** — "Son/Daughter" stated explicitly; highest-priority census item |
| 3 | pli_009 | Census | FamilySearch | 1900 | Thomas Flynn as "father" in Patrick's or a sibling's household |
| 4 | pli_010 | Vital/Marriage | FamilySearch (col. 1401638) | 1865–1882 | **Patrick's own marriage record** — Catholic registers named parents of both parties |
| 5 | pli_011 | Church/Baptism | FamilySearch (col. 1401638) | 1847–1880 | **Siblings' baptisms** — each names Thomas Flynn & wife as parents; godparents are FAN leads |
| 6 | pli_012 | Church/Marriage | FamilySearch (col. 1401638) | 1840–1870 | **Thomas & wife's marriage record** — confirms the couple, supplies mother's maiden name |
| 7 | pli_013 | Naturalization | FamilySearch / Ancestry | 1852–1900 | **Thomas Flynn's naturalization petition** — post-1906 form names wife & all children with birthplaces |

### Why each item is a FAN move

- **Items 1–3 (census):** The 1870 and 1880 searches are about reconstructing Thomas Flynn's *whole household* — wife, every child — not just confirming Patrick was there. The 1880 relationship column is the specific payoff. The 1900 search looks for Thomas Flynn residing *in Patrick's household*, which inverts the logic: it is Patrick's associates (his own household) that would then document the relationship explicitly.
- **Items 4, 5, 9–10 (marriage and death records of Patrick and his siblings):** These are records *about other people* (Patrick's spouse, Patrick's siblings) that incidentally name the parents. This is the core FAN principle — the evidence you need is embedded in records created about someone else.
- **Item 6 (Thomas & wife's marriage):** Required by the parentage planning standard; also supplies the mother's maiden name, which is needed to trace her separately and to evaluate any census household keyed to that name.
- **Items 7–8 (naturalization, land):** Legal instruments from Thomas Flynn's own adult life in Schuylkill County. Post-1906 naturalization petitions are the single most explicit family enumeration outside a census. Deeds add the wife's name via dower acknowledgment and bring in the witness FAN cluster.

- **Item 9/10 date window** — sized to Thomas Flynn's plausible reproductive years (~1840–1875), not Patrick's lifespan, so sibling death certs through ~1950 are in scope.
